This index covers all technical items - papers, correspondence, reviews, etc. - that appeared in this periodical during the year, and items from previous years that were commented upon or corrected in this year. Departments and other items may also be covered if they have been judged to have archival value. The Author Index contains the primary entry for each item, listed under the first author's name. The primary entry includes the coauthors' names, the title of the paper or other item, and its location, specified by the publication abbreviation, year, month, and inclusive pagination. The Subject Index contains entries describing the item under all appropriate subject headings, plus the first author's name, the publication abbreviation, month, and year, and inclusive pages. Note that the item title is found only under the primary entry in the Author Index.
IBM scientists have developed an experimental laser-enhanced electroplating technique that could eliminate the need for the overlaid masks currently employed in conventional IC fabrication.

The second edition of the Newman and Sproull's book is a welcome sight. A much more comprehensive text includes discussions of the work done in computer graphics since the first edition. For example, the new edition reflects the recent burgeoning of raster graphics techniques by devoting substantially larger sections to the subject. Discussion of software system construction is also a major consideration in the volume, likewise reflecting one of the major current concerns in the field of computer graphics.

A junior-senior level book, Arnold Allen's Probability, Statics, and Queueing Theory with Computer Science Applications would be quite useful as a text for the applied probability and statistics course in a computer science or engineering curriculum. It is also very suitable for self-study by practicing computer science data processing professionals.
MSP Inc. has added an IMS/DC interface for its Datamanager data dictionary system.

Designed for process control applications, Ramtek's FS 2500 color video display controller is a microprocessor-based character graphics system featuring a programmable display of 254 characters and 64 foreground/background color combinations or eight gray-scale levels.

In the last 20 years, the number of publications has increased so dramatically that one is tempted to ignore them all rather than sift through myriad pages, gleaning substance from between the lines. So it is not surprising that my reaction to hearing that another periodical was making its debut was less than mild enthusiasm. Although keenly aware of the need for complete yet concise material on robotics, I could not help but think that this journal would be just another addition to the layers of shelf-cluttering, dust-gathering landfill which has overrun the markets in recent years. But the monrent I opened the cover, I realized that this magazine was unique, in that it ushered in a new era in man's history–the age of robotics.

An antiskid brake control system that maintains vehicle stability and steerability during emergency braking has been developed by a team of automotive engineers from Robert Bosch GMBH, Stuttgart, West Germany, and, IC designers from American Micro-Systems, Inc., Santa Clara, California.

Scientists at IBM Research have used a computer to transcribe speech, composed of sentences drawn from a 1000-word vocabulary and read at a normal speaking pace, into printed form with what is believed to be the best accuracy yet obtained under complex experimental conditions–91 percent.

In an era in which writing compilers is still somewhat an art, Compiler Construction: Theory and Practice goes far toward transforming this art into a science. This book is not only an instructive manual on building compilers, it is also a superior reference book. Computer science students, especially those with some professional programming experience, and their professors will find it an excellent treatment of some of the most complex material in the undergraduate curriculam. Professional compiler writers will also find the book valuable.

Jean-Loup Baer's Computer Systems Architecture is one of the most complete treatises on computer architecture I've had the pleasure of reading. Its wide range of topics and references and the inclusion of exercises to test comprehension make it an ideal text for studies at both the undergraduate and graduate levels.

Using voice synthesis, the IBM Audio Typing Unit simulates actual speech, offering audio functions to assist a blind typist. Consisting of an audio keypad and console, the unit can be attached to the IBM Mag Card II, Mag Card/A, Memory, or Memory 100 host typewriter.

Histories of cryptography are apt to be episodic. For long periods of time nothing seems to be happening–but for good reasons. Cryptographic offices do not announce successful penetration of another nation's secrecy system. On the contrary, they guard this information so jealously that they hesitate even to use any intelligence gained through it, lest the other nation, realizing the discovery, should discontinue its use of the now transparent system.

Mead and Conway's Introduction to VLSI Systems is a survey of integrated circuit technology and VLSI system science. Presented in a manner more dependent on intuition than on rigorous lines of reasoning, the material may be easily understood by persons from a variety of backgrounds. By liberally using anecdotes and comparisons to everyday experience, the authors have made the text pleasurable reading; it should be recommended to those outside the computer and chip communities who wish to learn something about these fields without getting bogged down in details. The range of topics covered also make it ideal additional reading in computer science survey courses. Finally, this text removes some of the mystique of integrated circuit design by reassuring experienced logic designers, through numerous examples, that traditional design techniques and requirements still apply.

For persons in industry desiring a quick and concise introduction to data-base technology and data-base management systems, Database: A Professional's Primer is exactly that. Written for systems analysts, prommers, or managers who have no formal training in data-base systems, it imparts enough knowledge to let them discuss data-base concepts intelligently.

Providing increased speed and capacity, the new version ofNCR Corporation's Interactive Healthcare Information System operates under the IRX operating system on the company's I-8400 series systems po meet the needs of hospitals with up to 600beds.
An integrated desktop computer system featuring graphics computation, the Hewlett-Packard Series 9800 System 45C is capable of displaying results in up to 4913 colors on a CRT display.
According to Genisco Computers, the GCT-3032-8 graphics/imaging postprocessor significantly extends the capability of high-resolution (1280x1024x8) color or monochrome display systems.

Essentially a manual-load version of the SLT-80, the Dennison Kybe MLT-500 cleaner/tester for maintaining and evaluating 800-, 1600-, and 6250-bpi computer tapes differentiates between signal dropouts that are within a system's error correction routines and those that will cause an abort, a testing technique that emulates the tape transport's 1600-bpi error recognition routines.

An elevator goes up and down. That seems simple enough, but there is more to it, much more. Suppose we have a bank of elevators serving 15 or 16 rooms on each of the 34 floors in a busy downtown hotel. Suppose we have to be prepared to operate in the fire mode. Suppose we'd like to give priority to calls from certain floors. Maybe we'd like to keep a history of every move our elevators make for later analysis.

New York City's Arson-for-Profit information center now has instant access to data in the city's departments of Finance and Housing Development. Two Raytheon Data Systems PTS-2000 information display units and a shared character printer in Arson Strike Force offices are connected to IBM 370 host computers in the two city departments.

DI-3000 is a fully integrated, machine-independent system of 160 user-callable subroutines for building, viewing, interacting with, and manipulating computer graphics images. Developed by the authors of the DIGRAF package at the University of Colorado, DI-3000 is built upon the functional capabilities of the updated CORE Graphics System, described in the 1979 report of SIGGRAPH's Graphics Standards Planning Committee.

Designed to be a complete and Wellintegrated system, Artec Electronics' Centurion 8-bit microcomputer features 16K of internal PROM, 64K of RAM, a floppy disk controller, and a Digital Research CP/M operating system built on a shielded motherboard. Using a floating-point math chip, it can process data at a rate of 7 MHz.

With recent advances in technology, color CRT displays have become increasingly affordable and practical for viewing graphical information. For a variety of users, having hard copies of displayed images has also become beneficial and, in many cases, necessary. However, until recently high-quality fully saturated color hard copy has not been readily available. To meet this need, a simple technique has evolved within the past year that produces photographic prints instantly, using Polaroid 8 X 10 Polacolor 2 Land film as the output medium.

An excellent introduction to some basic techniques used frequently in AI systems, Principles of Artificial Intelligence by Nils J. Nilsson is well organized, with an orderly progression of topics. The book covers material not treated in the author's previous book.* Based on teaching notes for courses given at Stanford University and the University of Massachusetts at Amherst, the book is designed as a text for use in a one- or two-semester senior or first-year graduate course in AI.

HCR/Basic, an implementation of Basic which conforms completely to ANSI Standard X3.60-1978, allows PDP-11 users who run the Bell Labs Unix timesharing system to run or develop programs written in standard Basic.

Astronomers started out using the naked eye some 10,000 years ago, advanced to telescopes in the time of Galileo, and began serious observations in the infrared band of the electromagnetic spectrum only a generation ago. The computer-controlled infrared telescope of the University of Wyoming, located atop Jelm Mountain, was at the time of its installation (November 1977) the largest instrument specifically designed to operate in the 1- to 1000-micron (10,000-angstrom to 1-millimeter) wavelength range.

Chasen and Dow's text is a collection of selection guides for computer-aided design and manufacturing systems. Approaching CAD/CAM evaluation with a highly mechanical, "hand-holding" okbook of forms, checklists, and timetables the book appears geared toward nontechnical managers. Readers looking for a discussion of particular CAD/ CAM systems, trends, or technical information should look elsewhere (the Proceedings of the Design Automation Conference, for example).

Introduced by Pro-Log Corporation, the PM9074 generic personality module allows Series 90 PROM programmers to program Intel's high-speed 2732A HMOS EPROM. It will also accommodate other HMOS EPROMs and higher density PROMs as they are developed.

In a massive study of the migration patterns of Canada geese under way at Louisiana State University, scientists are using an IBM 3033 processor to locate clues to help conservationists redistribute the flocks of more than a million birds now wintering mostly in Missouri, Illinois, and Tennessee.
Designed for use primarily as a graphics computer peripheral, the Hewlett-Packard Model 1311B CRT display has a resolution of 60 lines/inch at center screen with minimum corner defocusing.

This instruction text for the Radio Shack Level II Basic language is written in the same easy-to-digest, step-by-step style as Lien's User's Manual for Level I, which accompanies each Radio Shack computer. Since the original manual is apt to be the TRS-80 user's first introduction to the use of a computer, Lien has included a "cut and paste" appendix to Learning Level II so that the beginner can use the introductory text as a guide to a Level II system with the appropriate material altered. This is certainly a diligent attempt to adapt the original support material to Level II equipment.

The UCLA Tissue Typing Laboratory is using Data General Corporation's Transaction Processing Management System in its kidney donor and recipient program. Functions performed by the laboratory include serum testing on potential transplant recipients, tissue typing, and creating correlation matrices and scattergrams.

Can a robot work on an aircraft production line? The answer, quite simply, is "yes." One robot is drilling and routing sheet metal parts on the production line of the F-16 fighter aircraft at Air Force Plant Number Four in Fort Worth, Texas, resulting in increased productivity and a reduction in manufacturing costs.

Faced with the need to produce complex, easily modifiable technical drawings as quickly as possible, Westinghouse Electric's Heavy Industry Motor Division turned to computer graphics. By installing Lockheed's CADAM–Computer Graphics Augmented Design and Manufacturing–system on an IBM S/370-138 with eight graphics terminals, the division tripled the productivity of its drafting department.
Harris Corporation's Model 5660/5661 disk drive subsytsem, based on Winchester technolody, provides 675M bytes of random access storage.
